item.title: Music gear companies open-source devices in response to AI vibe-coding
item.description:
Music gear companies open-source devices in response to AI vibe-coding

The emergence of powerful vibe-coding agents and tools has created chaos in the music gear world, forcing companies to determine how to respond to a wave of AI-aided custom firmwares and modding communities. While some manufacturers have remained silent, others have decided to embrace the trend by opening up their devices and providing tools for the community.

🔍 Overview

As it became clear that no piece of music gear was safe from AI tools and curious tinkerers, companies began making their devices open source. Major names like inMusic, the parent company of Akai, Moog, and Native Instruments, decided to “join ’em” rather than resist. Meanwhile, companies like Roland, Korg, Arturia, and Novation have yet to issue public statements on the matter.

⚙️ Key details

  • inMusic: inMusic CEO Jack O’Donnell stated the company will provide a toolbox and the inner workings of devices like the MPC or Sample so people can do what they want. This includes a recently launched SDK and several open-source devices, including the recently teased MPC Sample Key. Akai aims to walk a fine line by offering modders access while keeping products reliable for professionals, promising a “reset button” so users can experiment without losing their original setup.
  • Behringer: The company announced a slew of open-source devices, including a $150 clone of the MPC One called Kick, a clone of the E-mu SP-1200, the Anima DJ controller, the Ignite sequencer, and the Polykeys 61 MIDI controller. Launch dates for these products are currently unclear.
  • M-Vave: The company’s $70 pocketable clone of the Yamaha DX7 became popular due to its price and hackability, leading to more than a dozen custom firmwares. M-Vave responded by releasing an open-source firmware for developers and confirmed its successor, the FM-2, will also be open source.
  • Erica Synths: The company released the source code for its LXR-02 drum machine. Founder Ģirts Ozoliņš noted the sustainability of using one device with various options instead of buying multiple “plastic boxes,” while acknowledging that vibe coding does not offset the environmental impact of data centers.
  • Polyend: Open-sourced its line of Tracker grooveboxes and released the Endless guitar pedal last year, which allows users to vibe-code their own effects.
  • Elektron: The company banned links to custom firmware from its official forums, warning that modifications could brick machines, prevent updates, or affect warranty coverage. CPO Christian Alsing stated that while he is sympathetic to the hacker community and believes users have the right to modify their devices, he pushed back on accusations that the company is withholding features.

💡 Why it matters

The shift toward open-sourcing hardware and firmware reflects a strategic pivot in the music technology industry. Companies are balancing the potential for community innovation and sustainability against the risks of hardware instability and the environmental costs associated with AI development.

#vibe-coding #open-source #music-gear #firmware #modding

Source: Has vibe coding made open source the new normal for synths?

item.title: inMusic Opens Up Gear for Community Modding with Open‑Source Toolkits
item.description:
inMusic Opens Up Gear for Community Modding with Open‑Source Toolkits

inMusic, the parent company behind Akai, Moog, Native Instruments and others, announced that it will actively support the music‑gear modding community by releasing source code and development tools for several of its products.

🔍 Overview

  • inMusic decided to embrace the modding community.
  • The move follows a broader industry shift where companies are opening hardware for user‑driven innovation.

🛠️ Toolbox Details

  • In an interview with The Verge, inMusic CEO Jack O’Donnell said, “We’re going to provide a toolbox to the community, we’re going to provide the inner workings of, say, an MPC or Sample so that people can do what they want.”
  • The toolbox includes:
    • Open‑sourcing the code for the recently teased MPC Sample Key.
    • Providing an SDK that makes modifications easier and reduces the risk of “bricking your beloved sampler.”
  • O’Donnell added, “We’ll try to give them a reset button,” so that “They can experiment with it, and then not lose what they have.”

🎹 Products Being Open‑Sourced

Company Device Open‑Source Status
inMusic (Akai) MPC Sample Key Code released, SDK provided
Erica Synths LXR‑02 drum machine Source code released
Polyend Tracker grooveboxes Open‑sourced
Behringer Kick (MPC One clone) Announced open‑source
Behringer E‑mu SP‑1200 clone Announced open‑source
Behringer Anima DJ controller Announced open‑source
Behringer Ignite sequencer Announced open‑source
Behringer Polykeys 61 MIDI controller Announced open‑source

📅 Upcoming Events

  • inMusic plans a major presence at NAMM, the annual music‑manufacturer convention in Anaheim.
  • The company will host a Creator Lab where technically curious musicians can get hands‑on time hacking 22 new products from across its brands, including Moog devices.
  • O’Donnell noted that even analog‑centric Moog gear can be opened “if we open it up correctly,” which will involve “building a platform for devs to work around the analog parts of the circuit.”

🤝 Industry Context

  • Other companies have also embraced the modding community: Erica Synths, Polyend and Behringer have released source code or announced open‑source devices.
  • inMusic’s forums currently ban linking to hacks or modified firmware, warning that such changes could “brick” devices, prevent updates, or affect warranty coverage.
  • Elektron, while expressing mixed feelings, does not actively block the community.
  • O’Donnell explained, “you can try to wall them off, which is just a losing battle one … and so we want to embrace them.”
  • The consensus among manufacturers is that “there’s no going back now that vibe coding has upended the music gear world, and trying to stand in the way would be a mistake.”

#inMusic #modding #openSource #musicGear
